title: Digital Arrivals Card coming in 2027
body:
O.P.
Looks like the trial they have been running with Qantas was successful, and they are now planning to (mostly) replace the paper arrival card for all passengers arriving by air or sea.
https://www.abc.net.au/news/ 2026-07-13/digital-arrival-c ards-international-travellers-australia/106907440
From next year, the program will be expanded further to include all Australian international airports and seaports and will become available to all travellers — not just those flying Qantas — through a webform.
Details look similar to most other countries that have done this – fill in via a website (or similar) up to 3 days before arrival. Whilst I do think this is a great idea, I really do wonder how well this is going to work for a country that is so interested in biosecurity. People answering "Do you have nuts?" style questions 3 days before departure when they potentially have no idea what is in their bags will be a problem. New Zealand limits to 24 hours before departure which is better but likely still has the same issues.
According to that article, you will still be able to use the paper form if you'd prefer (but presumably only on arrival – I can't see the airlines giving them out).
The comments about asking airlines to build it into their own apps is an interesting idea I haven't seen before (outside of the Qantas trial) – it has the potential advantage of the fact the airline already has much of the details required so you don't need to re-enter them, likely negated by the fact that beyond Qantas and maybe one or two others I can't see the airlines wanting to take on the extra overhead of doing that.

Most other countries have had this for years, yet we have wasted millions on 2 or 3 failed attempts. And even now they want years to complete the rollout.

[User #742437061 postsTheDocWhirlpool Forums Addict] O.P.
durrr90 writes...
So you have to fill it out at least 3 days in advance or in the 3 days leading up to your departure?
Within 3 days, sometimes (incorrectly) stated as within 72 hours. In general the way it's implemented is that if you arrive on Friday, then you can fill it in on either Wednesday, Thursday or Friday. When you take into account things like flights that arrive just after midnight, and various time zones, it can all get a little complex – but in general the sites require you to select an arrival date, and they will only give the options of days that are within the valid '3 day' period.
The NZ one appears to be "24 hours from departure", but I haven't looked into exactly what that means (eg, departure of first flight? Or the actual flight into NZ?)
OrangeKnight writes...
About bloody time! The annoyance of hunting down a pen on a 9hr flight is annoying.
I fill in the arrival card at my hotel the night before. I always have a spare or two (just grab one next time you're going through immigration), so I fill one of those in, and then when they give me one when boarding/on the plane, it becomes my spare for next time. Makes things so much easier – although obviously it's only really for people that travel enough to make the planning worth it.
fwp writes...
Australian citizens shouldn't have to fill in a thing on arrival, that's how plenty of other countries handle it. The arrival card should be left for foreign visitors.
Based on my experience, this one is mixed. Some countries do require their citizens to fill out the form (eg, Singapore) whilst others don't (eg, Thailand). If only for the biosecurity issues, I can't see Australia ever not requiring Australian citizens to do something. Potentially it's a shorter process for Aussies (just like there's far fewer questions on the kiosks for Australian citizens than others), but it'll still need to be there.

The infrastructure is already there. If they haven't performance tested it at full volume yet then its not ready to roll out. I speak from 30+ years of working in IT project delivery and software testing.
